messages:
Jordan: Quick follow-up to the obs schema RFC — should cost attribution live as metric tags, span attrs, or logs? RFC: https://rwd/obs/rfc-cost-schema
Alex: I'd prefer minimal span attrs for realtime aggregation (model, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, billing_tier). then derive metrics from traces.
Maria: warning: including user_id/requester_id in spans will explode cardinality. keep high-cardinality in logs or event store only.
Sam: pushing all cost details into traces will balloon our ingest and storage costs. recommend two-tier approach: low-cardinality span attrs + separate cost events pipeline for full granularity.
Taylor: +1. also suggest normalizing enums for billing_tier/model_family to avoid tag permutations.
Jordan: example sketch of span attrs?
Taylor: sure, here's a minimal example:
```
span.attributes:
  model: "redwood-v1"
  model_family: "redwood"
  model_variant: "v1-quant"
  seq_len_bucket: "0-128"
  billing_tier: "dedicated"
  estimated_cost_usd: "0.0023"  # low precision string
```
Alex: note: keep estimated_cost as low-precision string/enum to avoid float noise in tag indices. compute exact cost in offline pipeline.
Maria: for rollout: disallow free-form model tags. add mapping table in onboard step to canonicalize names.
Sam: sampling plan: deterministic hash on request_id -> sample 1% full-span + 5% extended attrs. rest get only canonical tags. that keeps tail-analysis possible without blowing up costs.
observability-bot: pipeline-deploy: cost-events-producer v1 promoted to staging at 2026-02-15T18:22:11Z
Alex: action items: 1) add billing_tier & model_family enums to trace schema (Maria) 2) implement deterministic sampling in ingest (Sam) 3) build cost-events producer that writes detailed cost events to S3/kafka (Taylor) 4) RFC for retention/cold-storage pricing (Jordan)
Jordan: assigning owners as above. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with examples and a migration plan. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
